.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (line 28 shaped reward 0.6/0.2/0.2 behind zero-weight gates and functional floor)
evidence: Dimension weights in task/tests/scoring.toml lines 5-8 (functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2; gates render/constraints 0.0; floor functional 0.05) are byte-identical to the frozen template scoring.toml and match SKILL.md line 28 and the Internal Quality Checks E45 note; task score.py is identical to the template (diff clean), so reward = weighted mean only when gates pass and functional > 0.05. Per-criterion weights (parsed with tomllib): functional 16 binary criteria totalling 42.0 under an explicit rule (scored/functional/judge.toml lines 32-37: core legal 2.0, ordinary chat 1.5, small 1.0, summed per part). The brief's two stated top priorities (instruction.md para 2: walls and retention) carry the most mass: walls wall_every_route 4.0 + wall_mentions_and_links 4.0 + wall_added_live 2.0 = 10.0; retention deleted_and_expired_messages 4.0 + timer_changes 4.0 + hold_scope_and_release 2.0 = 10.0; plus persistence 2.0, search_and_transcript 4.0, signin_and_client_scope 3.0 - i.e. about 48% of functional mass on walls/retention and every 4.0 criterion is a two-or-three-part security/retention flow, while ordinary chat features (nested replies, safe formatting, message links, unread, live updates) sit at 1.5. Polish (6 x 1.0 binary keyboard/confirm/highlight/phone/refusal behaviours) and visual (likert: sidebar 2.0, retention marks 2.0, transcript 1.0, phone 1.0) weight retention-related craft highest. Non-functional maximum contribution is 0.4 and cannot be farmed by a non-working app: gates zero the reward, the functional floor needs > 2.1/42 (no single 1.5 or 2.0 criterion clears it alone), and every polish/visual criterion requires a working sign-in/send/edit/search/transcript (visual anchors score 0 when nothing renders). Plausible-broken-app probe: a pretty chat that passes only nested_replies + safe_formatting (3.0/42) clears the floor and caps at 0.6*0.071+0.4 = 0.443, while a plain app that passes all four access-control criteria (13/42) but no polish/visual earns 0.186; this inversion is a consequence of the template-controlled 0.6/0.2/0.2 split (SKILL.md line 28, AGENTS.md: preserve template-controlled settings), not a task-specific weight choice, so it is recorded rather than failed here (ranking is row 42/43). Conforming-alternative probe: no per-criterion weight penalises a legitimate design more than a functional defect; weights are by promise, not by golden-specific detail. Minor observations (not fails): client scope (walls-and-retention.md: 'The same goes for clients...') is weighted 1.5 as ordinary rather than 2.0 core; hold_scope_and_release bundles several hold promises (scope, delete refusal, partner-only, release-applies-timer) at a single 2.0 whereas timer_changes is 4.0 - hold survival under timers is additionally graded inside timer_changes and deleted_and_expired_messages, so total hold mass is reasonable. Risk=true because raw-evidence-index.json explicitly states reward discrimination/ranking runs on these bytes are absent, so the ordering consequences of these weights are unmeasured, and the 0.4 non-functional ceiling inversion above remains a template-level risk.
